leetcode.title: 486. Predict the Winner
leetcode.explanation:
#StreakQ #DP #GameTheory

We play from player 1 perspective and create a DP : dp[left][right] = p1score - p2score

Here left and right are, index of nums array. we use top down approach, to solve this.

The base condition: If left are right are same, we return nums[left]. since its the only value left.

Memo: if dp[left][right] exists, we return it

Now for computation: Take left number : so score willl be nums[left] - recursion(left + 1, right); Here left+1, right, means, p2 will take either from left + 1 or right, so we minus that

Same for right side. Now take max, since we want best for p1. dp[left][right] = max(leftside, rightside) and then we return dp[left][right]

we call this topDown with recursion(0, nums.length-1)

[Leetcode](https://leetcode.com/problems/predict-the-winner/)

leetcode.title: 877. Stone Game
leetcode.explanation:
[877. Stone Game](https://leetcode.com/problems/stone-game/description/)

#StreakQ  #DP  #GameTheory

In this question, we return true, if Alice win, though. Alice always wins, how?
Alice can decide whether "I'm going to collect all even-indexed piles" or "odd-indexed piles"

eg: [3,7,2,3] => even = 3 + 2 = 5, odd => 7+3 = 10

so alice can just take odd here, if even was bigger, alice would take even.
therefore alice always wins, so we can just return true for this question

leetcode.title: 1448. Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
leetcode.explanation:
[1448. Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree](https://leetcode.com/problems/count-good-nodes-in-binary-tree/description/)

[#Tree](https://leetcode.com/problem-list/tree/) Neetcode150

We keep track of max node value so far, when propagating using dfs.
1) If there is no node, just return
2) Check, if root.val is greater than max node value so far then increase good count.
3) if root.val is greater, than keep it as newMax
4) explore left branch, right branch using
 dfs(root.left, newMax) 
dfs(root.right, newMax)
5) call dfs(root, root.val) 
6) return good
